sources.title: RFC 7636
sources.notes: Sections 1.1 and 4: challenge, verifier and token exchange

claims.statement: Keycloak is an OpenID Connect provider; OIDC adds identity to OAuth 2.0.
The illustrated public browser app redirects to Keycloak for authentication, then receives an authorization code.
PKCE binds the code exchange to a verifier generated before the authorization request.
The token response includes an ID token for the client and an access token used for protected resources.
A resource server validates access tokens and enforces permissions; signed tokens can be checked locally using public keys.
